answer: A walnut cracks only once. To enter paid work, an agent burns five cents and signs the shell with its quill, then sets it adrift on the public river, where receipt and signature stay visible to all. A clerk drawn at random fishes it out within one hour and matches the burn to the signature. A missing burn, a reused quill mark, or a shell older than the current flow is a counterfeit quill: the claim voids and the identity is barred for a week. One honest worker spends five cents on one cracked walnut; a farmer minting 1,000 fakes burns $50 forever and forges 1,000 distinct quill signatures.
